G3186999.description: Žabljak (Cyrillic: Жабљак, pronounced [ʒâbʎaːk]) is a small town in the northern region of Montenegro. It has a population of 1,723. Žabljak is the seat of Žabljak Municipality (2011 population: 3,569).

G3188516.description: Ulcinj (Albanian: Ulqin) is a town in the coastal region of Montenegro and the capital of Ulcinj Municipality. It has an urban population of 11,488.

G3188584.description: Tuzi (Albanian: Tuz; Cyrillic: Тузи) is a small town in the central region of Montenegro, and the seat of Tuzi Municipality. It is located along a main road between the city of Podgorica and the Albanian border crossing, just a few kilometers north of Lake Skadar.

G3191631.description: Risan (Montenegrin: Рисан, pronounced [rîsan]) is a town in the Bay of Kotor, Montenegro. It traces its origins to the ancient settlement of Rhizon, the oldest settlement in the Bay of Kotor.

G3192576.description: Prčanj (Montenegrin: Прчањ, pronounced [př̩tʃaɲ]) is a small town along the Bay of Kotor, in southwestern Montenegro. According to the 2011 census, the town has a population of 1,128 people.

G3193044.description: Podgorica is the capital and largest city of Montenegro. The city is located in central Montenegro, at the confluence of Ribnica and Morača rivers, where the southern foothills of Dinaric Alps meet the northernmost part of Zeta Plain.

G3193131.description: Plužine (Cyrillic: Плужине, pronounced [plûʒinɛ]) is a town in Montenegro in the northern region. In 2023 it had a population of 1,102.

G3193161.description: Pljevlja (Montenegrin: Пљевља, pronounced [pʎêʋʎa]) is a town located in the Northern Region of Montenegro, situated along Ćehotina river. The town lies at an altitude of 770 m (2,530 ft).

G3193228.description: Plav (Montenegrin Cyrillic: Плав, Albanian: Plavë, Plava) is a town located in the Northern Region of Montenegro, situated along the Lim River, which originates from nearby Lake Plav, a glacial lake at the foot of the Prokletije mountains. It has a population of 3,717 (2011 census).

G3193504.description: Perast (Montenegrin: Perast) is a town in Coastal region of Montenegro. It is situated a few kilometres northwest of Kotor and is noted for its proximity to the islets of St.

G3194494.description: Nikšić (Cyrillic: Никшић, pronounced [nîkʃit͡ɕ]) is Montenegro's second-largest city, with an urban population of 66,700 as of the 2023 census. It lies in the western region of the country, at the heart of the expansive Nikšić field, nestled at the base of Trebjesa Hill.

G3197538.description: Kotor (Montenegrin Cyrillic: Котор, pronounced [kɔ̌tɔr]), historically known as Cattaro (from Italian, pronounced [ˈkattaro]), is a town in Coastal region of Montenegro. It is located in a secluded part of the Bay of Kotor.

G3197896.description: Kolašin (Cyrillic: Колашин, pronounced [kɔlǎʃin]) is a town in northern Montenegro. It has a population of 2,418 (2023 census).

G3199071.description: Berane (Montenegrin/Serbian Cyrillic: Беране) is a town in Montenegro in the northern region. It is former administrative centre of the Ivangrad District.

G3199161.description: Igalo (Montenegrin: Игало, Serbian: Игало) is a small town in the Herceg Novi Municipality of Montenegro. It is accessible via the E65/E80 north headed to Dubrovnik, Croatia.

G3199394.description: Herceg Novi (Cyrillic: Херцег Нови, pronounced [xěrtseɡ nôviː]) is a town in Coastal region of Montenegro located at the Western entrance to the Bay of Kotor and at the foot of Mount Orjen. It is the administrative center of the Herceg Novi Municipality with around 33,000 inhabitants.

G3199463.description: Gusinje (Cyrillic: Гусиње, pronounced [ɡǔsiɲe]; Albanian: Gucia) is a small town in Montenegro in the northern region. According to the 2011 census, the town has a population of 1,673 and is the administrative center of Gusinje Municipality.

G3200422.description: Golubovci (Montenegrin: Голубовци, pronounced [ɡǒluboʋtsi]) is a small town in the new Zeta Municipality of Montenegro. Until 2022, it was part of Podgorica Municipality.

G3202194.description: Danilovgrad (Cyrillic: Даниловград) is a town in central Montenegro. It has a population of 6,852, according to the 2011 census.

G3202641.description: Cetinje (Montenegrin Cyrillic: Цетиње, pronounced [t͡sětiɲe]) is a town in Montenegro. It is the former royal capital (Montenegrin: prijestonica / приjестоница) of Montenegro and is the location of several national institutions, including the official residence of the president of Montenegro.

G3203106.description: Budva (Cyrillic: Будва, pronounced [bûːdv̞a] or [bûdv̞a]) is a town in the Coastal region of Montenegro. It had 17,479 inhabitants as of 2023, and is the centre of Budva Municipality.

G3204176.description: Bijelo Polje (Cyrillic: Бијело Поље, pronounced [bîjeloː pôʎe], literally White Field) is a town located in the Northern Region of Montenegro, situated along Lim River. It has an urban population of 12,900 (2011 census).

G3204214.description: Bijela (Montenegrin Cyrillic: Бијела, pronounced [bîjɛlaː]) is a coastal town in the municipality of Herceg Novi, Montenegro. It is also located north of Herceg Novi, by the Verige strait in the Bay of Kotor.

G3204388.description: Bečići (Cyrillic: Бечићи, pronounced [bɛ̂tʃitɕi]) is a town in the municipality of Budva, Montenegro. It is located south-east of Budva, and has 895 permanent residents (2011 census).

G3204509.description: Bar (Montenegrin: Bar, Бар, pronounced [bâr], Italian: Antivari, Albanian: Tivari) is a town and seaport in Coastal region of Montenegro. It is the capital of the Bar Municipality and a centre for tourism.

G3204816.description: Andrijevica (Cyrillic: Андријевица, pronounced [andrǐjɛv̞it͡sa]) is a town in Montenegro in the northern region and it is the seat of Andrijevica Municipality. According to the 2023 Census of Montenegro, it had a population of 988.

G3220594.description: Petnjica (Montenegrin Cyrillic: Петњица) is a town in Montenegro in the northern region, and the center of Petnjica Municipality. Petnjica regained its municipality status on May 28, 2013, which it previously had from 1945 to 1957, when it was merged with the Berane Municipality.

G3318253.description: Škaljari is a small town in the municipality of Kotor, Montenegro. It is located just south of the town of Kotor.

G3318488.description: Šušanj (Montenegrin: Шушањ, pronounced [ʃûːʃaɲ]) is a small town in the municipality of Bar, Montenegro. A 2011 census put the population at 2,630.[1]

G786234.description: Rožaje (Montenegrin Cyrillic: Рожаје, pronounced [rɔ̂ʒajɛ]; Albanian: Rozhajë, pronounced [roʒajə]) is a town located in the Northern Region of Montenegro, situated along the Ibar river. The town is the cultural center of the Bosniaks in Montenegro.
